title: Gold Holds Drop as Middle East Fighting Stokes Inflation Fears
summary: Gold held a loss as the spreading conflict in the Middle East stoked fears that further energy supply disruptions could keep inflation elevated and increase the prospects for interest-rate hikes.

title: BNY's LaRusse Sees Scope for Bond Market Relief Rally
summary: April LaRusse, co-head of global client portfolio management at BNY Investments, says it is too early to confidently call a peak in Treasury yields. Speaking on "The Asia Trade," LaRusse says current market pricing for roughly three rate hikes looks excessive, leaving room for a relief rally if the Middle East conflict eases or labor market data weakens. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Australia Regulator Halts Another Credit Fund Amid Crackdown
summary: Australia’s securities regulator temporarily barred Fidante Partners Ltd. from offering units in a credit fund, extending a clampdown on private credit investments amid concerns over risks to investors.

title: RBA Raised Key Rate to Counter Upside Price Risk, Remains Alert
summary: Australia’s central bank raised its key interest rate two weeks ago because upside risks to inflation were coming to pass and waiting could prove costly, while adding the outlook would be heavily influenced by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Oct. 13
summary: Oil edged lower following three days of gains that were driven by concern the widening war in the Middle East could hamper a recovery in supply from the region.

title: Malaysian King Buys Stake in Miner Expanding Into Rare Earths

title: Albertsons Seeks More Than $9 Billion for Busted Kroger Deal
summary: Albertsons Cos. is demanding that Kroger Co. pay more than $9 billion for the collapse of what would have been the largest US grocery chain merger in history.

title: Fmr. Fed Governor Betsy Duke on CPI Amid Bank Results
summary: Betsy Duke, Former Fed governor and Former Wells Fargo Chair, says investors should pay closest attention to Fed officials’ comments this week. She argues that a single economic data point is unlikely to shift the outlook significantly, noting that Kevin Morris has emphasized watching trends rather than any one reading. She speaks with Scarlet Fu & Hema Parmar on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: BlackRock Turns Bullish on Short-Term Bonds, Downgrades Stocks
summary: BlackRock Inc.’s research unit has turned more bullish US Treasuries, unwinding a “mainstay” underweight stance for most of the past six years, as yields climbed to the highest levels in more than two decades.

title: How China Is Changing AI
summary:
As calls for an AI slowdown mount, Chinese and US governments are taking different approaches to AI development. Our latest episode comes a week ahead of Presidents Trump and Xi's meeting and compares the trajectory of China's AI models against their US counterparts.

In this episode of Bloomberg Tech: Asia, Shery Ahn speaks with Bloomberg Intelligence's Rob Lea and Bloomberg Economics' Michael Deng to examine the factors that enable or hinder China's AI advancement. We also hear from Phancy Group, a Chinese AI firm deeply embedded in the country's ecosystem. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Why China Generates Too Much Power
summary: China is racing to power a future of artificial intelligence and robots with renewables. But as it builds more electricity capacity than ever before, it faces a new challenge: whether the grid can keep up. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Why the Houthis Are So Hard to Defeat
summary:
After four years of relative calm, the war pitting Yemen’s Houthi militia against the country’s internationally recognized government and its backer Saudi Arabia is back on. Announcing the start of a full-scale military campaign against the Houthis, the Saudi-led force said on social media on October 4th that the goal is to “eliminate” the group.

Bloomberg's Veena Ali-Khan examines why the Houthis are so hard to defeat. She speaks with hosts Businessweek Daily hosts Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)
